reachable: Yes — verified by execution on a reconstructed cups layout, not by reading. The head adds `contrib` at `pred[:, 0:2m:2]` with `m = min(n_cmd, (L+1)//2)`, which covers the read command of every row including the deepest (unlike the r2 head it contrasts itself with). At the scored slot the read `s_i = ka_i^T M` is taken strictly before that slot's write, `ka_i` and `g_out_i` are functions of the command embedding alone, and M is built only from slots < i (all of which have their observation present in the cups layout). The obs-present gate `info` multiplies only the WRITE value, so the fatal 'gated on an observation that is absent at the read' pattern does not occur: measured head contribution at rpos was 0.05-0.12 per row, and it changed when an earlier move command embedding was perturbed with the read command held identical (arm sensitivity). Perturbing the padded post-read observation slot changed the scored prediction by exactly 0.0. Gradient: at init the main loss reaches out_scale (1.4e-3) and the aux reaches arg_trunk/src_ext/dst_shift/path_key/info_gate/rec_gate/erase_gate; move_gate has exactly zero gradient at init because ka==kb makes (s-d) identically zero, but dst_shift receives gradient through d_i, so the symmetry breaks immediately — a real 40-step _train run drove cos(ka,kb) to 0.84 and out_scale off zero. The transport aux mines 21 real examples from 8 trajectories, so it is not an inert loss.
solves_outside_model: No. The head parses no command strings anywhere; it consumes only tok/types/key_pad embeddings, and the genome's stream is baseline_interleave (unmodified M.collate), so the read token is untouched. The train-time aux mines slots using pairwise squared distances between observation and command EMBEDDINGS computed from the batch tensors under no_grad — that is sample/loss selection, the legitimate kind. Its target o_j is the observation at the supervised slot, which the memory read at slot j cannot see (M is built from slots < j), and aux_loss never runs at eval. The batcher r2_routedepth_tilt_readcollision_blocks DOES parse mv/cat strings to compute hop depth and read-collision neighbourhoods, but make_batcher returns only a list of integer indices and never mutates the sequences — sample selection, also legitimate. There is no path by which a Python-resolved move chain reaches the model as input at scoring time.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says. I executed the checks rather than reading them: the two-address update rule matches the hypothesis' formula to 4e-7 against an independent reimplementation; dst_shift zero-init makes ka==kb bitwise and the wrapped net bit-identical to the unwrapped net at init; the read is taken before the write and is causal (perturbing obs_2 leaves reads 0-2 untouched); the contribution lands on the scored read command of every row of a cups-shaped batch and is sensitive to earlier move commands with the read command fixed; the aux mines 21 genuine 'content resurfaces at a different path after a silent step' slots from 8 real trajectories, and its 'mutation' slots are almost exactly the routing commands. Every measured data figure the author stated is exact — 724 steps, 24 trajectories, cat 365 / mv 172 / ls 106 / cat> 30 / cat>> 51, 'cwd=/ exit=0' x227 and 'cwd=/data exit=0' x35 (262 of 724), all 253 routing observations contentless, ~11 silent observations per 32-step trajectory, and zero nonconforming src-first/dst-second routing commands. No command strings are parsed in the head; nothing resolved outside the model reaches it as input. The one structural quirk worth knowing is that move_gate has exactly zero gradient at initialisation (s-d is identically zero when ka==kb) but dst_shift does not, so the mechanism self-starts — confirmed by a 40-step training run. Four inaccuracies, all minor and all in rationale about OTHER programs rather than in what this code does: the parents did have a head (this one embeds it, as the hypothesis later admits); the partner arch r22 uses two keys per command, not one, though it still never transports a stored value; r19's routing write is a blend of observation and a same-address transition, not the raw observation; and the r2_dualaddress_move_transport contrast holds only for the deepest rows of a cups batch, not for every row. None of these change what is being scored or what the archived description will mean.

divergences.claim: "CROSSOVER: parent arch ... x partner batcher ..., joined by a new head that both parents lacked."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both the parent and the crossover partner carry head = r18_transition_forwardmodel_consistency (BRIEF.md lines for both genomes). The new head is a new IMPL, but it is not filling an empty axis — it embeds the parent's head verbatim as its `_fm_terms`, which the hypothesis itself states 27 lines later ("The parent head's forward-model consistency is kept").
divergences.evidence: evolve/rounds/r4/slot16-head/BRIEF.md: parent genome lists `head r18_transition_forwardmodel_consistency`; partner genome (line 263) lists the same. Diff of _fm_terms against evolve/chunks/head/r18_transition_forwardmodel_consistency.py: identical mining (same-path cosine > 0.60, change_floor 0.25, sim_ki*sim_kj*change weighting, topk 512, cos 0.10 / mse 0.02).

divergences.claim: "Both programs address memory with ONE key per command."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The partner arch r22_retrieval_composition_renderer uses SEPARATE read and write projections per command (`q_file = file_read(x_cmd)` vs `k_file = file_write(x_cmd)`; `q_path = path_read(h_cmd0)` vs `k_path = path_write(h_cmd0)`) — two keys per command. The load-bearing part of the claim is still correct: the write VALUE is `value_file = cat([obs_tok, ctx])` / `value_path = obs_tok`, i.e. the step's own observation, never a value read at another address.

divergences.claim: "the value a routing step writes is its own observation, which the paragraph above shows is a content-free constant" (about r19)
divergences.what_the_code_does: r19 writes `v_i = (1-w_i)*base_i + w_i*delta` where `delta = self._transition(s_pre, x_cmd[:,i,:])`, i.e. a blend of the observation with a command-conditioned transform of the content already at the SAME address. It is not the raw observation. The essential claim (single address, no cross-address transport) is nonetheless correct: `mem = decay*mem + bmm(pi, corr)` writes at the same `pi` it read from.

divergences.claim: "the archived r2_dualaddress_move_transport iterates n = L//2 slots and adds its contribution to cmd_view[:, :n]; on an odd-length stream that is every command EXCEPT the scored one."
divergences.what_the_code_does: On the cups layout the batch is one tensor with Lmax = 2*max_r + 1 shared across windows of DIFFERENT depth. n = L//2 = max_r, so cmd_view[:, :max_r] excludes only command index max_r. Rows whose read sits at r < max_r — the majority of windows — do receive r2's contribution at their scored slot. The contrast is therefore materially overstated, though it is a claim about a third-party archived impl, not about this candidate's own behaviour (which correctly indexes (L+1)//2 and was verified to reach every row's read).
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/head/r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py lines 106, 176-179; evolve/cups_probe.py build_cups_layout lines 106-128 (Lmax = 2*max(w["r"]) + 1, per-row rpos = 2*r).
